_comment: A Content Blocks Collection creates its own table. Left alone, 250 elements
with repeatable children would create well over a hundred near-identical
tables — Desiderio learned this and merged 29 of them into 12. These eight
cover what an Astryx-shaped catalog repeats, and every element that needs a
list of that shape points at the same table with shareAcrossTables.
Mergeability is decided by what a child MEANS, not by which columns happen
to line up: a testimonial and a feature both have a title and a text, and
they still stay apart, because an editor filling one expects different
things from an editor filling the other.

nav-item.purpose: A link in a list: menus, footers, tabs, tables of contents, link cards.

icon-lead.purpose: Icon, title and a sentence — the repeated unit of every feature and benefit grid.

metric-item.purpose: One number with its label, and optionally what it is compared against.

quote-item.purpose: A testimonial or review: what was said, by whom, and their standing.

person-item.purpose: A person: portrait, name, role, a line about them, and where to reach them.

logo-item.purpose: A client or partner mark, optionally linked.

qa-item.purpose: A question and its answer — accordions, FAQs, glossaries.

label-value.purpose: A row of a specification, comparison or plan-feature table.

media-card.purpose: A card with its own picture: link cards, slides, partner tiles, anything where the image belongs to the item rather than to the band.
media-card._note: icon-lead carries an icon and logo-item only a mark, so neither can hold a picture card. This is the type to reach for whenever each item needs its own image.

title._note: Never call this 'label' — Content Blocks reserves that identifier.

date._note: A real date rather than free text, so it can be formatted per language and sorted.

included._note: Whether this row's feature is part of the plan.
